verifications.claim: Artemis II will follow a ~10-day, figure-eight path.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'over the course of about a 10-day mission'; R3: 'heading to the moon in a figure-eight pattern'; R5: '10-day flight'
verifications.reasoning: Directly supported by duration in R1/R5 and figure-eight path in R3.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will launch from Kennedy Space Center (FL).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, Florida'; R3: 'Kennedy Space Center, Fla.'; R4: 'Kennedy Space Center in Florida'; R5: 'Kennedy Space Center near Cape Canaveral, Florida'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources explicitly state launch site.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will conduct a crewed flyby of the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first flight with crew aboard'; R2: 'launch four astronauts... loop around the Moon'; R3: 'fly by the lunar far side'; R4: 'orbit the moon during NASA's Artemis II mission, ... flyby'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm crewed mission looping/flying by Moon.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will return to a Pacific Ocean splashdown.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R4: 'trained in a large pool for their recovery in the Pacific Ocean'
verifications.reasoning: Mentions Pacific recovery training for Artemis II crew, but not explicitly 'splashdown' or confirmed return plan.

verifications.claim: Orion spacecraft will perform initial Earth orbits for systems checks.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'into Earth orbit'; R3: 'fly two orbits around Earth'; R1: 'confirm all of the spacecraft’s systems operate as designed'
verifications.reasoning: Directly states initial Earth orbits and systems checks.

verifications.claim: Orion spacecraft will use a free-return trajectory.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'The mission follows a free-return trajectory'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly states free-return trajectory for the mission.

verifications.claim: The free-return trajectory loops around the far side of the Moon roughly 3,000–9,000 miles above the surface.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'fly by the lunar far side at around 3,000-9,000 miles above the surface'
verifications.reasoning: Exact distance and far side flyby match.

verifications.claim: The free-return trajectory will slingshot back to Earth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'free-return trajectory that uses the gravity of the Earth and Moon to naturally guide the crew home'
verifications.reasoning: Gravity assist ('slingshot') implied in free-return description.

verifications.claim: Space Launch System (SLS) rocket lifts off from Kennedy Space Center (FL).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and the ground systems at Kennedy Space Center'; R5: 'NASA's massive Space Launch System rocket... from Kennedy Space Center'

verifications.claim: Space Launch System (SLS) rocket sends Orion into an initial high-Earth orbit to check systems.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'confirm all of the spacecraft’s systems'; R2: 'launch... into Earth orbit'
verifications.reasoning: SLS sends to Earth orbit for checks, but 'high-Earth orbit' not specified (likely low Earth orbit).

verifications.claim: A burn from the Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage (ICPS) will propel the crew toward the Moon.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: ICPS not mentioned in any reference.

verifications.claim: Orion will pass behind the far side of the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'loop around the Moon'; R3: 'fly by the lunar far side'

verifications.claim: Orion will use the Moon's gravity to assist in a free-return loop back toward Earth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'free-return trajectory that uses the gravity of the Earth and Moon to naturally guide the crew home'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly uses Moon's gravity for return.

verifications.claim: The service module will separate from the crew module before atmospheric re-entry.
verifications.label: OMITTED

verifications.claim: The launch is designed to be visible from parts of Florida, Georgia, and the surrounding region within the first 70 seconds.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'Launch + 70 seconds... Visibility may include Savannah, Georgia'; 'most of Florida... to parts of Georgia'
verifications.reasoning: Visibility map explicitly covers Florida, Georgia up to 70 seconds.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is currently planned for 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Released Tuesday, January 27, 2026'; R4: 'set to launch... on Wednesday, April 1'; R5: 'April 1, 2026'

verifications.claim: Artemis II will be the first crewed flight to leave low Earth orbit since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'first time in over 50 years that astronauts have been sent to explore the moon'; R4: 'long wait since the agency's last Apollo mission in 1972'
verifications.reasoning: Confirms first crewed deep space since Apollo 1972.
